findings.title: Malformed report rows can escape the report loader
findings.description: `BatchReport.load()` casts `items` to a list of dictionaries without validating its shape. A valid JSON file containing an item such as `null` or a string reaches `BatchItemRecord.from_json()`, where `.get()` raises `AttributeError`. That exception is not converted to `BatchReportLoadError`, so item resume can crash instead of returning a clear rejection for a malformed report.

findings.title: A failed JSON report write can leave Markdown out of sync
findings.description: `write()` replaces the Markdown report before the JSON report. If the JSON replacement fails, the Markdown contains the new records while the JSON—used by item resume—remains stale. The failed-write test checks that the old JSON remains intact, but does not check that the Markdown report remains consistent.

findings.title: Pipeline load failures are misclassified during item resume
findings.description: `load_pipeline(state.pipeline)` can fail if a saved run refers to a removed or invalid pipeline. A missing pipeline is caught by the outer `OSError` handler and reported as `HALTED` with a “cannot write the batch report” message; validation errors may escape `resume_item` entirely. These should be handled as a validation refusal with an accurate message and exit code.
